itinerary.activity: Embarkation; the ship sails at 19:00. Athens is worth arriving early for — the Acropolis at opening time, before the heat and the crowds, then aboard for sailaway.
The small-port stop the big ships skip — gateway to the Mani peninsula and Mystras' Byzantine hillside, with waterfront tavernas doing exactly what they've always done. In port 08:00–17:30.
Twenty minutes from Ancient Olympia — the original stadium, the workshop of Phidias, and olive groves that have watched the whole story. In port 08:00–18:00.
Ionian and Adriatic water. The Nova class keeps its open side to the sea — this is the day to claim it.

The sail into the Bay of Kotor is the day's event in itself — fjord-like walls closing in on a medieval town. The ship stays late, so the climb to St. John's fortress and dinner in the old town both fit.
A city built inside Diocletian's retirement palace — the cathedral was his mausoleum. Morning in the palace lanes, afternoon on the Riva or out to Trogir. In port 08:00–18:00.
Roman forum, the Sea Organ playing whatever the Adriatic sends it, and a sunset Hitchcock called the finest he'd seen. In port 08:00–19:00.
Morning arrival at Venice's lagoon port and disembarkation. If there was ever a place to add post-cruise nights, it's this one — I build that with you before you sail.
